# Recovery Assertion

## H1 — Goal

Fix `run.sh` so it prints today’s year using a portable invocation compatible with GNU and BSD `date`, then echoes `done`.

## H2 — Handoff Revision

The governing handoff revision is `aded72058dfbc62127c64d80ecb07afff6dd83c9992f13dd47e1ae0efcddb236`, based on commit `cf5b6a0b142a524afd2a983bea553f5b5d151776`.

## H3 — Verified State

Slice `S1` is verified and must not be redone. Journal sequence 7 records a Conductor-authored verification receipt distinct from the executor, bound to Gate and independent-review evidence.

## H4 — Unverified / In-Progress State

Slice `S2` is prepared but unverified; no `S2` action or verification receipt is recorded. The current target-file observation is:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
date +%Y 2>/dev/null || date -j +%Y
echo not-done
```

This worktree observation, including any uncommitted state, is observation only and does not establish progress or completion.

## H5 — Pending Action

The pending `S2` outcome is to edit only `run.sh` so it ends with `echo done` instead of `echo not-done` and exits successfully. No deterministic executor-side check is declared.

## H6 — Blockers

No blocker is recorded. Shell execution and agent spawning are prohibited constraints, not blockers.

## H7 — Legal Next Action

The sole legal next task action is one governed `Edit` or `Write` operation on `run.sh` that changes the final echo from `not-done` to `done`, without modifying the already verified year-printing work.

## H8 — Non-Goals / Forbidden Scope

No work beyond the stated task is authorized. Changes under `.tad/scripts/`, `.claude/`, or `.tad/hooks/` are forbidden. Other slices, hidden acceptance, scope expansion, redoing `S1`, and declaring overall completion are outside authority.

## S1 — Why the Next Action Is Legal

The active slice contract is `S2`, its required outcome explicitly changes the ending of `run.sh` to echo `done`, `run.sh` is its only allowed path, and `Edit` and `Write` are authorized tool classes.

## S2 — Why Verified Work Must Not Be Redone

`S1` has a ledger-recorded verification receipt written by `conductor-blake-p2`, whose identity differs from the executor, after Gate and independent review evidence. The packet expressly forbids repeating verified work.

## S3 — Why Blind Retry / Self-Completion Is Unavailable

The earlier action belongs to verified `S1` and cannot be retried. No failed `S2` action exists to retry. A checkpoint or executor assertion cannot advance verification; only a distinct Conductor can issue a bound verification receipt after Gate and independent review pass.

## S4 — What Is Rejected

Rejected actions include changing the portable date invocation, touching any path except `run.sh`, using Shell/Bash, spawning agents, inspecting hidden acceptance, modifying forbidden directories, starting another slice, treating observed or uncommitted content as completed work, or declaring the goal complete.
